title: Reykjavik University speech recognizer replaces first-stage manual transcription of Icelandic parliamentary speeches at Althingi
summary: Reykjavik University's ASR has produced Althingi's first-draft speech transcripts in production since January 2019 (Interspeech 2019).
account: Alþingi, the Icelandic parliament, has collaborated with Reykjavik University since 2016 to replace the first, manual stage of transcribing members' speeches with automatic speech recognition. The Interspeech 2019 paper by Helgadóttir and colleagues states: 'The system entered a test phase in October 2018, and has been in production since January 2019.' The production system used a time-delay deep neural network acoustic model with an n-gram language model (8.52% word error rate on the test set; 15.0 ± 6.0% over 625 speeches in the wild), and Althingi's transcribers graded 77% of transcripts as Good. Morgunblaðið reported on 16 November 2019 that about 640 hours of speeches had been transcribed. The date observed is 1 January 2019, the first day of the production month.
purpose: Built specifically to transcribe Althingi speeches for post-editing and publication; this benefit was that purpose.
system: Althingi ASR system (time-delay deep neural network acoustic model, n-gram language model, punctuation and paragraph models)
developer: Reykjavik University Language and Voice Lab (ASR for Althingi project)
taxonomy_note: Candidate c asked for an endangered or low-resource language; the fetched sources do not use the term 'low-resource' for Icelandic, so that framing is the verifier's rather than the sources'. Reykjavík is given as Alþingi's seat; none of the cited sources states where Alþingi sits, and the city appears in them only in Reykjavik University's name.

ratings.reason: Althingi replaced first-stage manual transcription with ASR drafts graded Good for 77% of speeches, with about 640 hours transcribed by November 2019.
Vísir reported on 4 March 2018 that the recognizer was released under an open-source license for Icelandic-language developers; a small, diffuse benefit.

ai_role.statement: The ASR produces the first-draft transcript; Althingi's editors still post-edit, so the benefit is editing time saved rather than full automation.
